messages.content: Find me all the classical concerts near Berlin and Paris happening next Friday, and I am interested only in those with available parking.

function.name: concert_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby concerts based on specific criteria like genre and availability of parking. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city where the user wants to find a concert.

date.description: The date on which the user wants to attend a concert.

genre.description: The genre of music of the concert.

We need to call the function concert_find_nearby twice: once for Berlin, once for Paris. The date is next Friday. We need to compute next Friday's date. Today is 2026-11-04. Let's calculate next Friday. 2026-11-04 is a Thursday? Let's check: 2026-11-04. We can approximate: 2026-01-01 was a Monday? Actually let's quickly compute: 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Wait, 2025-12-31 was a Saturday? Let's do quick: 2025-01-01 was a Wednesday (since 2020-01-01 was Wednesday, 2021-01-01 was Friday, 2022-01-01 was Saturday, 2023-01-01 was Sunday, 2024-01-01 was Monday, 2025-01-01 was Wednesday). So 2025-12-31 is Tuesday? Actually 2025-12-31 would be Tuesday because 2025-01-01 was Wednesday, so 2025-12-31 is also Wednesday? Wait, 2025-01-01 Wednesday, then 2025-12-31 is also Wednesday? Because 2025 is not leap year, so 365 days later, same day. So 2025-12-31 Wednesday. Then 2026-01-01 is Thursday. So 2026-01-01 Thursday. So 2026-11-04: we need to count days from Jan 1 to Nov 4. 2026 is not leap year? 2026 is not divisible by 4, so normal year. Days until November 4: Jan(31) + Feb(28)=59, Mar(31)=90, Apr(30)=120, May(31)=151, Jun(30)=181, Jul(31)=212, Aug(31)=243, Sep(30)=273, Oct(31)=304, plus 4 days into Nov=308. So 308 days after Jan 1. Jan 1 is Thursday. Add 308 mod 7 = 308 % 7 = 0? 7*44=308. So same weekday as Jan 1: Thursday. So 2026-11-04 is Thursday. Next Friday is 2026-11-05. So date is 2026-11-05.

Now we call function for location "Berlin", date "2026-11-05", genre "Classical", amenities ["Parking"]. And similarly for "Paris".
